brent.label: Brent crude — Wed Jun 3 intraday ~$97.98 (TT News)
brent.change: ▲ +$3.00 / +3.16% vs Jun 1 ($94.98); +2.1% on the day (TT News) — a third straight session higher; oil up ~10% on the week. ~+38% above the Feb 27 baseline.
brent.tooltip: Brent climbed a third straight session as the US and Iran traded strikes around the Strait of Hormuz — TT News put the front-month near $97.98 (+2.1%) intraday June 3. SOURCE SPREAD (not picked silently): TradingEconomics $96.89, Fortune spot $101.36 (8:45am ET); the official settle was pending at compile time. Baseline Feb 27 $71.00 — Day 96 war premium ≈ +$26.98 (+38%); oil is up ~10% on the week but still well below the war's ~$126 April peak. Sources: TT News, TradingEconomics, Fortune.

wti.label: WTI crude — Wed Jun 3 above $95 (TradingEconomics)
wti.change: ▲ vs Jun 1 ($92.54) — rose for a third session on the Hormuz risk premium; sixth straight weekly US crude drawdown.
wti.tooltip: NYMEX WTI rose for a third straight session, trading above $95 on June 3 (TradingEconomics) as US-Iran exchanges around the Strait of Hormuz lifted the risk premium. US commercial crude inventories drew for a sixth straight week (−6.8M to −7.97M bbl). Baseline Feb 27 $66.50 — Day 96 war premium ≈ +$28.68 (+43%). Sources: TradingEconomics, EIA.

gas.label: AAA national average, regular unleaded — June 2, 2026 (Day 95; held into Day 96)
gas.change: ▼ −3.2¢ vs June 1 ($4.322); +$1.30 vs $2.99 Feb 28 baseline. Pump prices eased off the May peak even as crude rebounded toward $100.
gas.tooltip: AAA gasprices.aaa.com national average $4.29 on Tuesday June 2 (Day 95), down from $4.322 (June 1) and well off the May 6 peak of $4.536 (Fox Business). ~+43% above the $2.99 Feb 28 baseline; the May peak stayed below AAA's all-time record of $5.016 (June 14, 2022). Five states (AK, HI, NV, OR, WA) remain above $5; California is highest near $6.16. GasBuddy's Patrick De Haan: 'We won't see those [peak] levels until potentially mid-to-late 2027'; relief runs 2-3 weeks behind crude. Brown University (Costs of War): Americans have spent ~$401 more per household on gas and diesel since the war began. Source: gasprices.aaa.com.

sp500.label: S&P 500 — Wed Jun 3 close (Day 96): −0.74%, snapped a nine-day win streak
sp500.change: ▼ −0.74% to ~7,553 — broke a nine-day record-setting win streak as Gulf escalation lifted oil and Treasury yields; Dow −620.72 (−1.21%), Nasdaq −0.89%.
sp500.tooltip: S&P 500 fell 0.74% on June 3, snapping a NINE-DAY record-setting winning streak (CNN framed it as the longest since 2004; CNBC said a potential 10th straight day would be the longest in 'more than three decades' — use 'nine-day,' do not assert 'three decades' as fact). Dow Jones −620.72 (−1.21%), Nasdaq Composite −0.89%. The reversal came as Iran's strike on Kuwait International Airport and renewed Bahrain attacks pushed Brent +2.1% toward $98 and lifted Treasury yields. War-beneficiaries led: defense (LMT +14.9% YTD) and oil majors (XOM/CVX ~+11% during the crisis); airlines and cruise lines fell. After hours, weak guidance sank Broadcom −13% and CrowdStrike −10%. The prior session (June 2) set a record 7,609.78 (+0.13%). Sources: CNBC, TheStreet, CNN.

daily_cost.label: Daily War Burn (CSIS ceasefire band, $M) — Day 96
daily_cost.change: Ticked up to ~$150M/day on June 3's renewed exchanges (tanker Hellfire strike, drone shootdowns, Kuwait/Bahrain intercepts) — still in the CSIS ceasefire band, far below the major-combat $500M-$2B/day.
daily_cost.tooltip: The current ceasefire-period daily burn is ~$150M (CSIS/Cancian band), elevated from the ~$95M quiet floor by June 3's kinetic exchanges — a US Hellfire strike on an Iranian tanker, three one-way attack drones downed, and interceptor expenditure around Kuwait/Bahrain. CONTEXT: the Pentagon's own accrual methodology runs ~$1B/day (first six days $11.3B, ~$1B/day thereafter), which would imply ~$100B over the war versus the $29B official cumulative — the two Pentagon framings do not reconcile (see total cost). Burn could re-spike toward the kinetic-phase $500M-$2B/day if Trump orders resumed strikes, or step down if an MoU is signed and the blockade unwinds. Sources: CSIS, Pentagon.

total_cost.label: Cumulative US war cost (Pentagon official, $B) — Day 96
total_cost.change: Pentagon official ~$29B (Acting Comptroller Hurst, May 12) — the last official figure; any Day-96 extrapolation beyond $29B is UNVERIFIED (no Pentagon update since May 12).
total_cost.tooltip: Last official Pentagon figure ~$29B direct military (Acting Comptroller Jules W. Hurst III, May 12 House Approps; up from $25B munitions-only) — excludes base-repair and force-flow costs; NO update since May 12, so any higher Day-96 number is UNVERIFIED. Reported separately (do not merge): the broader 'Iran War Cost' portal estimate exceeds $100B including regional/maintenance; independent estimates include Semler/SPRI ~$72B and Penn Wharton ~$42.5B; Harvard's Linda Bilmes projects ~$1T lifetime. Separately, the consumer fuel burden (ITEP, May 31) ran ~$46.5B / $347.72 per household. Sources: Pentagon (Hurst), Brown Costs of War, ITEP.

history.headline: Project Freedom kicks off; Iran retaliates with missile/drone barrage on UAE; Brent +5.8% to $114.44, oil's biggest single-day jump since early April

Pentagon (Hegseth/Caine) confirms 'ceasefire is not over'; Project Freedom Day 2; oil pares (Brent intraday $112.90, -1.4%); UAE airspace partial closure May 4-11; AAA gas $4.483 (+49.9% vs baseline); 22,500 mariners on 1,550+ vessels stranded Persian Gulf
Rubio: 'Epic Fury concluded'; Trump pauses Project Freedom citing 14-point MOU progress; oil collapses 8-9%, S&P fresh record; Araghchi meets Wang Yi in Beijing
Iran reviews 14-point MoU; PGSA institutionalizes Hormuz tolls; Israel breaks Lebanon truce in Beirut killing Radwan commander Ballout; F/A-18 disables M/T Hasna in first aerial blockade interdiction

Hormuz tit-for-tat continues; F/A-18 from Bush disables 2 more Iranian tankers (Sea Star III + Sevda); Iran reviews US response to 14-pt MoU; Kharg oil slick (~45 km²) detected; UAE intercepts new Iranian salvo; markets rebound to S&P 500 record on jobs beat

Saudi/Kuwait restored US base/airspace access; Iran MoU reply slipped past 48-hr window; Israel killed 24+ in Lebanon Saturday; Rubio + Witkoff met Qatari PM Al-Thani in Miami; weekend carry on markets (S&P record held); Ford CSG Day 316 deployed (post-Vietnam record)

Diplomacy collapses publicly: Iran's 14-pt reply via Pakistan rejected by Trump as 'TOTALLY UNACCEPTABLE'; Kuwait/UAE/Qatar all hit by drones at dawn; bulk carrier struck off Doha; Energy Sec Wright threatens military Hormuz option 'next few days'

Diplomatic rupture deepens: Trump calls ceasefire 'on life support,' Iran reply 'garbage,' 'didn't even finish reading it'; oil +3% to $104.21; S&P fresh intraday ATH 7,426; Lebanon MoPH 2,869 (+86 since Day 71); Boxer ARG ETA slips to week of May 18

April CPI 3.8% (highest since May 2023); oil reclaims $100; Hegseth/Caine grilled by bipartisan Congress on $29B cost and weapons stocks; Ford CSG Day 323 westbound Atlantic; Trump departs for Beijing with Iran 'on massive life support'; no new strikes on Iranian homeland (4th consecutive day)

Day 75 — Trump lands in Beijing; 5-day kinetic pause holds; PPI shock +6% YoY; S&P new record 7,444.25; Chinese COSCO VLCC Yuan Hua Hu exits Hormuz past Larak Island — first Chinese supertanker outbound transit since blockade tightening; Senate confirms Warsh to Fed Board; Ford CSG Day 324 mid-Atlantic targeting end-of-month Norfolk

Day 76 — Trump-Xi Beijing Day 1: joint position 'Strait of Hormuz must remain open' + 'Iran can never have a nuclear weapon'; Iran grants ~30 Chinese vessels safe passage via IRGC northern corridor (no tolls); S&P/Nasdaq intraday records, Dow reclaims 50,000; Day 6 of zero-kinetic streak (longest of war); Lebanon talks Round 3 opens Washington (Karam-Dermer-Rubio); UNICEF flags 200 children killed in Lebanon since March 2; Ford CSG Day 325 mid-Atlantic

Day 77 — Trump-Xi Beijing Day 2 closes no-breakthrough; Trump aboard AF1 'losing patience' with Iran, floats 'cleanup work'; bond rout — 30Y >5.12%, 10Y 4.595%, CME Dec hike prob 44%; S&P -1.24% (worst day in weeks), energy sole green sector; Day 7 of zero-kinetic streak (longest of war); Israel-Lebanon Round 3 concludes no-breakthrough, IDF orders evac of 5 southern villages, ceasefire expires Sunday; Ford CSG D-1 from Norfolk arrival Saturday

Day 78 — Kosovo 78-day tie (NATO Allied Force); USS Ford CSG returns Norfolk after 326-day deployment (longest post-Vietnam), Presidential Unit Citation awarded; Hormuz tanker seized off Fujairah + Indian cargo ship sunk off Oman (5/14); Iran 5-condition demand (reparations + Hormuz sovereignty) — non-starter for Washington; Trump-Xi closes vague on Iran, no joint statement; Israel-Lebanon ceasefire EXTENDED +45 days, Pentagon security track May 29; NYT: US-Israel intensifying renewed-strike prep 'as soon as next week' (UNVERIFIED); Day 8 zero-kinetic streak on Iran (39 days since Apr 7); markets weekend carry — S&P -1.24%, Brent +3.35%, WTI +4.20%, 30Y UST 5.121%

Day 79 — BARAKAH STRUCK: drone hits UAE's Barakah Nuclear Plant electrical generator (no radiological release, no casualties; Unit 3 on emergency diesel per IAEA); first nuclear-facility attack on a Gulf state during the war; Saudi separately intercepts 3 drones from Iraqi airspace; Trump 'there won't be anything left of them. TIME IS OF THE ESSENCE!'; Axios/Ravid: Trump convenes Situation Room Tue May 19 to review military options; Netanyahu cabinet 'we are prepared for any scenario'; AP: Israel 'coordinating with US about possible resumption'; IRGC threatens to 'deactivate' US Gulf bases; Day 9 zero-kinetic streak on Iran (40 days since Apr 7) — LONGEST OF WAR, exceeds Kosovo 78-day Allied Force record; Israeli strikes kill ≥5 in 5 southern Lebanon villages (Tayr Felsay, Tayr Debba, Az-Zrariyah, Jebchit, Jouaiya); Lebanon CF extended +45 days (May 15); Bloomberg Hormuz tracker: ZERO Sun-morning transits; Jones Act waiver expires today; daily-burn RECALIBRATED to $95M/day (CSIS standby) post-Ford CSG return; AAA gas $4.513 (-0.4¢ d/d); markets closed Sun, futures gap-down expected on CME 6 PM ET reopen

Day 80 — TRUMP POSTPONES TUESDAY ATTACK at request of Saudi MBS, UAE MBZ, and Qatari Emir Tamim citing 'serious negotiations'; FIRST public disclosure of any imminent strike package since Apr 8 ceasefire (NO CENTCOM corroboration; UNVERIFIED per CBS News); Trump directs Hegseth + JCS Chair Caine to 'be prepared to go forward with a full, large scale assault of Iran, on a moment's notice'; LEBANESE DEATH TOLL CROSSES 3,000 — MoPH formal announcement: 3,020 killed since Mar 2 incl. 292 women + 211 children; Israeli airstrike on Baalbek killed Palestinian Islamic Jihad commander Wael Abdel Halim + 17-yr daughter post-midnight; Iran-US talks continue via Pakistani mediator (Iran FM spokesperson Baghaei); Iran FM Baqaei: Tehran 'committed to ensuring transit through Strait of Hormuz' / 'in continuous contact with Oman'; Israeli troops intercept Gaza-bound flotilla off Cyprus; Day 10 zero-kinetic streak on Iran (41 days since Apr 7) — LONGEST OF WAR; markets mixed S&P 500 7,403.05 (-0.07%), Dow +0.32%, Nasdaq -0.51%, 10Y UST 4.13% 52-WK HIGH; energy XLE +1.92%, defense ITA $218.93 lagging despite Epic Fury spend; Brent $110.13 intraday (range $107.71-$111.34), WTI $106.22 (range $99.18-$108) — official settles PENDING; AAA gas $4.515 (+0.2¢ d/d); IEA Birol (G7 Paris): inventories 'depleting very fast … several weeks, declining rapidly' — IEA May OMR 246 mb drawdown Mar-Apr (steepest on record), -3.9 mbpd 2026 supply forecast; USS Theodore Roosevelt home San Diego May 14 (USNI Fleet Tracker 5/18); Lincoln + Bush remain two-carrier blockade steady-state in CENTCOM AOR + Tripoli ARG; USS Pioneer + USS Chief MCMs Sasebo→CENTCOM en route (Hormuz mine-threat signaling); cumulative cost ~$31.7B per Pentagon $29B (Hurst May 12) + 6 days × $95M standby

Day 81 — STRIKE 'AN HOUR AWAY' STOOD DOWN: Trump tells reporters at the White House 'We were all set to go… It would have been happening right now' — confirming the Tuesday May 19 strike package was operationally ready before postponement at the personal request of Tamim/MBS/MBZ; postponement framed as 'two or three days'; NSC convened the Situation Room May 19; BARAKAH ATTRIBUTION FINALIZED — UAE Ministry of Defence confirms via technical tracking that the three drones which struck the Barakah Nuclear Power Plant on May 17 'all originated from Iraqi territory' (UAE handled +6 more drones from Iraq over 48 hrs; AP/WaPo: 'likely signaling Iranian-backed Shiite militias'; no group claim of responsibility); CENTCOM blockade now 85 commercial vessels redirected ('15,000+ troops, 200+ aircraft, 20 warships'); Project Freedom escort sorties still UNCONFIRMED resumed (Lloyd's List: no Western-allied transits since May 4); Iran submits updated peace proposal via mediators — White House views as insufficient; VP Vance invokes Cold War 'domino theory'; Day 11 zero-kinetic streak on Iran (42 days since Apr 7) — LONGEST OF WAR; markets fall a third straight session — S&P 500 7,353.61 (-0.67%), Dow 49,363.88 (-0.65%), Nasdaq 25,870.71 (-0.84%), 30Y UST briefly 5.19% (highest in ~19 years); Brent $110.59 (-1.35%), WTI $103.49 (-0.85%) — oil retreats modestly on the postponement; AAA gas $4.533 (+1.8¢ d/d); war-cost spread widens — Pentagon $29B / CBS ~$50B / Semler $71.8B; cumulative ~$31.8B per Pentagon $29B (Hurst May 12) + 7 days × $95M standby

Day 82 — POSTPONEMENT HOLDS / SENATE WAR-POWERS BREAKTHROUGH 50-47: Trump's May 18 postponement of the scheduled May 19 strike held through May 20; Trump told Coast Guard Academy graduates in New London the U.S. is 'in no hurry' but 'may have to hit them even harder. But maybe not.' Day 12 of zero-kinetic streak on Iran (LONGEST OF WAR; 43 days since Apr 7). SENATE advanced Sen. Tim Kaine's war-powers resolution 50-47 (May 19) — first procedural win after seven failures; four GOP defectors (Collins, Murkowski, Paul, Cassidy — who flipped three days after losing his Trump-endorsed primary). IRAN POSTURE HARDENED: FM Araghchi warned of 'many more surprises'; the IRGC threatened renewed war would spread 'beyond the region'; FM spokesman Baghaei flatly denied direct U.S.-Iran negotiations. UAE confirmed the May 17 Barakah drones came from Iraqi territory and intercepted six more Iraq-origin drones over 48 hours. Xi met Putin in Beijing — joint statement demanded an immediate ceasefire. CENTCOM blockade 91 vessels redirected. LEBANON ceasefire effectively unraveled — Israeli strikes May 19 killed ≥19 in southern Lebanon (incl. 4 women, 3 children); 8th IDF soldier KIA since the April 16 truce. MARKETS: oil sold off — Brent ~$107, WTI cracked below $100 (~-5%); S&P 500 rebounded +1.08% to ~7,433, Dow +1.31%, Nasdaq +1.54%; AAA gas $4.555 (+2.2¢ d/d, +52.3% vs baseline); cumulative ~$31.9B per Pentagon $29B (Hurst May 12) + 8 days × $95M standby

Day 83 — MUNIR IN TEHRAN / TRUMP DEMANDS IRAN'S URANIUM / DOW RECORD CLOSE: Pakistan Army Chief Field Marshal Asim Munir visited Tehran for talks as Pakistan's mediation intensified; Iran's Foreign Ministry confirmed it is reviewing the latest U.S. proposal. The diplomatic file narrowed to uranium custody — Trump vowed to seize Iran's HEU stockpile while Tehran counter-offered to 'downblend' the material inside Iran. Sec. State Rubio cited 'some encouraging signs' but called a Strait of Hormuz toll system an unacceptable redline that 'would make a diplomatic deal unfeasible'; Iran announced a 'Persian Gulf Strait Authority' and revealed Iran-Oman toll talks. House GOP leaders punted the war-powers vote into June after defections threatened to pass it. Day 13 of the zero-kinetic streak on Iran (LONGEST OF WAR; 44 days since Apr 7) — the postponed May 19 strike never ran. LEBANON: Lebanese MoH cumulative reached 3,073 (31+ killed in 24 hours); Israeli strikes May 20 on the Tyre district killed 8. MARKETS: Brent settled $102.58 (-2.3%), WTI $96.35 (-1.94%); the Dow set a RECORD CLOSE 50,285.66 (+0.55%) on IBM +12.43% (CHIPS Act quantum award); S&P 500 7,445.72 (+0.17%); Nasdaq 26,293.10 (+0.09%); AAA gas $4.56 — a four-year Memorial Day high; UMich consumer sentiment hit an all-time low 48.2; cumulative ~$32.0B per Pentagon $29B (Hurst May 12) + 9 days × $95M standby

Day 84 — MUNIR LANDS IN TEHRAN / IRAN SAYS US PLAN 'NARROWED THE GAPS' BUT URANIUM HANDOVER 'KILLS THE DEAL' / S&P 8TH STRAIGHT WEEKLY GAIN — LONGEST SINCE DEC 2023 / DOW SETS NEW RECORD CLOSE / UMICH SENTIMENT 44.8 ALL-TIME LOW / DAY 14 OF ZERO-KINETIC STREAK ON IRAN: Pakistan Army Chief Field Marshal Asim Munir landed in Tehran with high-level security delegation and was received by Iranian Interior Minister Eskandar Momeni; Pakistani Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi continued meetings with FM Araghchi to deliberate draft agreements ending the war. Qatar formally assumed secondary-mediator role despite the wartime Iranian strike on Ras Laffan LNG. Iran (ISNA via Bloomberg) said the US text has 'narrowed the gaps to some extent' while 'deep and significant' differences remain — Tehran calls the demand to hand over enriched uranium a 'dealkiller.' Trump (Oval Office): 'We'll probably destroy [the enriched uranium] after we get it, but we're not going to let them have it.' Sec. Rubio cited 'some good signs' but said Washington retains 'other options.' House GOP PULLED the Iran War Powers resolution that appeared to have the votes to pass — Rep. Meeks: 'We had the votes without question and they knew it.' Acting Navy Sec. Hung Cao told the Senate the US has PAUSED the $14B Taiwan arms sale to preserve munitions for the Iran campaign. UMich final May Consumer Sentiment 44.8 — a new all-time low in the 78-year series (prior trough June 2022 at 50.0). AAA national gas $4.552 — Memorial Day weekend pump prices at four-year highs, 9¢ below the June 2022 record $4.61; AAA forecasts a record 45M Memorial Day travelers. MARKETS: S&P 500 7,473.47 (+0.37%) — 8th consecutive weekly gain (longest since the 9-week run ending Dec 29, 2023); Dow Jones 50,579.70 NEW RECORD CLOSE (+0.58%); Nasdaq 26,343.97; Russell 2000 2,869.23; VIX 16.70. Brent settled $103.94 (+1.33%) but down ~4% on the week; WTI $97.12 (+0.67%) but down ~3% on the week. Hormuz transits 2 vessels (IMF PortWatch via Straits.live, ~2.1% of pre-crisis baseline); 1,550+ vessels stranded, 22,500 mariners trapped. LEBANON: IDF strike near the Lebanon-Israel border killed 2 (Al Jazeera Day-84 live blog). Cumulative ~$32.1B per Pentagon $29B (Hurst May 12) + 10 days × $95M standby; CBS unofficial 'closer to $50B'; Bilmes projects $1T lifetime.

Day 85 — TRUMP DECLARES MoU 'LARGELY NEGOTIATED' / 14-CLAUSE FRAMEWORK REVEALED (NUCLEAR DEFERRED) / MUNIR DEPARTS TEHRAN / CENTCOM HITS 100-SHIP BLOCKADE MILESTONE / ISRAEL HITS ~15 SOUTHERN LEBANON VILLAGES / IDF SGT. HAMBURGER KIA (22ND IN LEBANON WAR) / DAY 15 OF ZERO-KINETIC STREAK ON IRAN. Trump on Truth Social (~17:00 ET): 'An Agreement has been largely negotiated, subject to finalization between the United States of America, the Islamic Republic of Iran, and the various other Countries… Final aspects and details of the Deal are currently being discussed, and will be announced shortly' — characterized as a 'Memorandum of Understanding pertaining to PEACE,' said the Strait of Hormuz would be reopened. Iran FM spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei (state TV / IRIB / IRNA): the framework is a 14-clause MoU providing a 30-60-day window for follow-on negotiations covering ending the war on all fronts (incl. Lebanon), the Strait of Hormuz, the US naval blockade ('US maritime piracy'), release of frozen Iranian assets, and sanctions relief — nuclear program explicitly NOT in the initial MoU. Pakistani Field Marshal Asim Munir left Tehran after meetings — Pakistani military said discussions produced 'encouraging progress toward a final understanding.' Trump multilateral phone calls with Saudi MBS, UAE MBZ, Qatari Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman, Pakistani PM Sharif and Field Marshal Munir, Turkish Erdoğan, Egyptian Sisi, Jordan, Bahrain, + separate Netanyahu call. VP JD Vance recalled from Ohio, SecDef Hegseth from West Point graduation, to Washington. CENTCOM (May 23 press release): 100 commercial vessels redirected, 4 disabled, 26 humanitarian aid ships permitted through since Apr 13 blockade began — 15,000+ service members and 200+ aircraft and warships, two CSGs (Lincoln + Bush) + MEU. Adm. Brad Cooper: 'allowing zero trade into and out of Iranian ports which has squeezed Iran economically.' LEBANON: Israeli airstrikes May 23 on multiple locations after IDF issued evacuation warnings to ~15 villages (Lebanon NNA via RFE/RL). IDF Staff Sgt. NOAM HAMBURGER, 22 — killed by Hezbollah drone strike near Lebanon border May 22, announcement May 23 — 22nd IDF KIA in Lebanon war. Markets closed Saturday — carry-forward Friday closes; AAA holiday-travel survey (Stacey Barber, May 11): record 45M Americans travelling ≥50 miles over the long weekend. Hegseth (West Point speech): U.S. Army hit its 2026 recruiting goal of 61,500 four months early. Cumulative ~$32.2B per Pentagon $29B (Hurst May 12) + 11 days × $95M standby.

Day 86 — TRUMP 'DON'T RUSH' REVERSAL / NETANYAHU DEMANDS DISMANTLEMENT + EMERGENCY CABINET / ASIAN FUTURES OPEN SHARPLY LOWER (BRENT -5.2% TO ~$98.12, WTI ~$92) / IRAN EXECUTES MOJTABA KIAN (FIRST WARTIME-ESPIONAGE EXECUTION) / IRAN CLAIMS ORBITER DRONE DOWNED (UNVERIFIED, IDF 'NOT FAMILIAR') / BAHRAIN COURT SENTENCES 9 TO LIFE OVER IRGC TIES / DAY 16 OF ZERO-KINETIC STREAK ON IRAN. Trump on Truth Social Sunday: 'I have informed my representatives not to rush into a deal in that time is on our side. The Blockade will remain in full force and effect until an agreement is reached, certified, and signed. Both sides must take their time and get it right.' Compared the working deal to Obama's JCPOA as 'THE EXACT OPPOSITE.' Senior US administration official to NBC News: 'The Iran agreement will not be signed today, but there has been progress on a deal'; separate US official to Axios said deal is '95% there,' with negotiators 'haggling over language' on Iran's enriched uranium stockpile and Hormuz arrangements. Iran President Masoud Pezeshkian (state TV / IRNA): 'We are ready to assure the world that we are not seeking nuclear weapons. We are not seeking instability in the region'; framed decisions inside Supreme National Security Council with permission of Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei. PM Netanyahu (X / Israeli statement): 'any final agreement with Iran must eliminate the nuclear threat entirely. This means dismantling Iran's uranium enrichment facilities and removing enriched nuclear material from its territory… Iran will never have a bomb.' IDF Chief of Staff Lt. Gen. Eyal Zamir approved operational plans for 'continued combat in the Northern Command region on the border with Lebanon'; emergency Israeli cabinet convened Sunday night amid alarm at deal terms. Iranian state media (Tasnim/Fars) contradicted Trump's Hormuz framing: Strait 'will not return to its pre-war status,' would remain under Iran's 'monopoly and discretion'; Iran demands $12B in frozen Qatar funds as Phase-1 MoU precondition. SecState Rubio (in New Delhi): 'There is the possibility that, over the next few hours, the world will get some good news, at least in regard to the straits.' MARKETS: U.S. closed (Memorial Day weekend; Monday holiday). ASIAN FUTURES OPENED SHARPLY LOWER late Sunday: Brent intraday low ~$98.12 (-5.2%), WTI ~$92 (Bloomberg/Fortune May 24 18:59 ET) on deal optimism — Kevin Hassett (Fox News Sunday): 'We expect energy prices, as soon as there's a deal, to plummet.' Iran executes Mojtaba Kian (Mizan News) — first known wartime espionage execution. Iran's Mehr News Agency claimed Iranian air defenses downed an Israeli-made Orbiter UAV over Hormozgan; IDF said 'NOT familiar with the incident' (UNVERIFIED). Hezbollah FPV drone detonated inside Israel — no injuries (IDF, Times of Israel). Bahrain court sentenced 9 to LIFE in prison and 2 to 3 years over IRGC ties — follows May 9 arrest of 41 individuals. Republican blowback: Sen. Cruz, Sen. Graham, ex-Sec. Pompeo all hammered the framework. Standard Chartered: SPR drew down 9.9 mb week-ended May 15 (largest weekly release on record); total SPR 374 mb. Watson Institute (Brown — Jeff Colgan): cumulative extra U.S. consumer fuel costs since war start now top $40B, more than $300/household. Cumulative ~$32.3B per Pentagon $29B (Hurst May 12) + 12 days × $95M standby.

Day 87 (MEMORIAL DAY) — CENTCOM 'SELF-DEFENSE' STRIKES NEAR BANDAR ABBAS END 16-DAY ZERO-KINETIC STREAK / TRUMP HONORS 13 EPIC FURY KIA AT ARLINGTON / RUBIO FRAMEWORK '95% THERE' / TRUMP DEMANDS ABRAHAM ACCORDS / NETANYAHU TO 'INTENSIFY' LEBANON STRIKES / OIL FUTURES DOWN ~5-6% INTRADAY / AAA GAS 4.507 4-YEAR MEMORIAL DAY HIGH / LEBANON CUMULATIVE 3,185 (+62 WEEKEND) / LAPID: DEAL 'A DISASTER': CENTCOM (Capt. Tim Hawkins, May 25): 'U.S. forces conducted self-defense strikes in southern Iran today to protect our troops from threats posed by Iranian forces. Targets included missile launch sites and Iranian boats attempting to emplace mines. U.S. Central Command continues to defend our forces while using restraint during the ongoing ceasefire.' Targets: Iranian missile launch sites, Iranian boats attempting to emplace mines, and an Iranian SAM site near Bandar Abbas (explosions also near Sirik and Jask). U.S. official: scope 'very small'; Iran's Mehr news agency said situation 'was under control.' Most significant U.S. kinetic action inside Iran since April 8 ceasefire; NO formal change to ceasefire status declared. President Trump at Arlington National Cemetery: 'In Operation Epic Fury, we lost 13 wonderful souls, wonderful special people' — explicit executive confirmation of US KIA = 13; SecWar Hegseth ('the 13 souls of Epic Fury') and CJCS Caine also delivered Memorial Day remarks invoking the operation. SecState Rubio (NYT May 24): framework '95% there'; haggling over 'language' on Iran's nuclear stockpile and Hormuz transit rights — 'You can't do a nuclear thing in 72 hours on the back of a napkin.' Trump reportedly gave Iran '5 to 7 days' to finalize a nuclear deal (Fox News May 24). Trump (Truth Social May 25): Abraham Accords MANDATORY for Saudi Arabia, Pakistan, Turkey, Egypt, Jordan as condition of Iran peace deal; threatened renewed military action 'bigger and stronger than ever before' if no deal; softened position on Iranian uranium — could be destroyed 'in place' or 'another acceptable location' with IAEA oversight, a shift from prior demand for transfer to the U.S. Netanyahu video May 25: Israel to 'intensify' Hezbollah strikes — 'I have instructed them to press the pedal even harder'; expanded Lebanon ground operations 'coordinated' with U.S. in 'near future' (Israeli source via CNN). Israel opposition leader Yair Lapid (Jerusalem press conference May 25): emerging agreement 'a disaster'; truce one of the greatest 'political disasters in all of our history.' Israel reportedly preparing for elections within ~4 months. Republican blowback continues from Day 86 (Cruz, Graham, Pompeo). Rubio-Lavrov phone call on Ukraine, U.S.-Russia relations, and Iran (Pravda USA citing RIA Novosti, May 25). Pakistani mediator reportedly told China that an agreement was nearing (Trading Economics May 25). UK Royal Fleet Auxiliary RFA Lyme Bay (Gibraltar) preparing for Strait of Hormuz mine-clearing deployment once a deal is reached (AP via Fox May 24). India began buying oil from Latin America and Africa due to Hormuz situation (Reuters via May 25 wire). LEBANON: Lebanese MoPH May 25 cumulative 3,185 killed / 9,633 wounded (+62 over May 23-25 weekend; +110 vs prior dashboard reading 3,075). May 23: 3,123 killed (+20 incl. 5 Al-Baqbouq, 9 Sir al-Gharbiya Nabatieh district, 1 al-Rafid Rashaya al-Wadi); IDF major killed May 23 (22nd IDF KIA in Lebanon war). IRAN: official Foundation of Martyrs figure 3,468 STALE since Apr 19 (~36 days old); HRANA 3,636 (Apr 7) carry remains primary tracker value. Mizan judiciary executed Mojtaba Kian May 24 — first known wartime espionage execution. MARKETS: U.S. cash closed Memorial Day federal holiday. Friday May 22 carry: S&P 7,473.47 (8th straight weekly gain — longest since Dec 2023), Dow 50,579.70 record, Nasdaq 26,343.97, ITA $225.41 (+1.00% Fri), VIX 16.59. Monday futures: WTI ~$91 intraday low (-5-6%), Brent ~$94.82 intraday low ('lowest since April 2026' — Trading Economics); equity futures rose; Euro STOXX 50 +1.75%. AAA national gas $4.507 — Memorial Day Monday four-year high (AAA landing-page banner: 'Memorial Day Weekend Gas Prices Reach Four-Year Highs'); +50.7% vs $2.99 baseline; ~10¢ below June 2022 record $4.61. State extremes May 25: CA ~$6.116, HI $5.641, D.C. $4.661, OK ~$3.98. CONGRESSIONAL: May 21 evening GOP called off Iran war-powers vote 'on the verge of passing' (AP); May 24 Republicans 'pan Trump's emerging proposal' to end the war. Rep. Thomas Massie (R-KY) on NBC Meet the Press May 24: 'Gas is almost $5 a gallon, diesel is almost $6 a gallon, and the farmers here in Kentucky can't afford the fertilizer to put on their fields.' Cumulative ~$32.4B per Pentagon $29B (Hurst May 12) + 13 days × $95M standby; CBS unofficial 'closer to $50B'; Bilmes $1T lifetime.

Day 88 — CENTCOM SELF-DEFENSE STRIKES OVERNIGHT (LARAK MINE-LAYING BOATS + BANDAR ABBAS SAM); 3 IRGC NAVY KIA NAMED; IRGC CLAIMS MQ-9 SHOOTDOWN (US: 'NO AIRCRAFT HIT'); RUBIO (JAIPUR): DEAL 'WILL TAKE A FEW DAYS' — QATAR TALKS ONGOING; IRAN BEGINS LIFTING 87-DAY NET BLACKOUT (NETBLOCKS: 'LONGEST IN MODERN HISTORY'); S&P RECORD 7,519.12 (+0.61%); NASDAQ RECORD 26,656.18 (+1.19%); MICRON +19% TOPS $1T; CONFERENCE BOARD CONFIDENCE 93.1 (-0.7); BRENT +3.58% TO $99.58; WTI -2.81% TO $93.89; AAA GAS $4.491 (-1.6¢); MASHGHARA STRIKE KILLS 11–12 IN BEKAA: CENTCOM (Capt. Tim Hawkins, statement carried May 25→26): 'U.S. forces conducted self-defense strikes in southern Iran today to protect our troops from threats posed by Iranian forces… continues to defend our forces while using restraint during the ongoing ceasefire.' Targets: 2× IRGC Navy vessels reportedly laying mines south of Larak Island + 1× SAM site Bandar Abbas. Iran International (citing SNN) named 3 IRGC Navy KIA: Abbas Eslami, Ghodrat Zarnagari, Abdolreza Golzari (Pravda/Tasnim: 4; Al Jazeera: 'several'). Iran's Mehr News: situation 'under control'; FM Baghaei: 'flagrant violation' of Apr 8 ceasefire — Iran ' reserves the legitimate and definite right' to respond (IRGC via IRNA/Fars). IRGC claim: 1× MQ-9 shot down + 'fired upon' 2nd MQ-9, RQ-4 Global Hawk, F-35 'forcing them to retreat' — US official to NBC News/Fox: 'no US aircraft were hit'; CENTCOM silent on platform losses; if confirmed, 25th MQ-9 lost in war. SecState Rubio (Jaipur press call): 'There were some talks going on in Qatar today, so we'll see if we can make progress. I think it's a lot of talking back and forth going on about specific language in the initial document, so it'll take a few days… The straits have to be open. They're going to be open one way or the other.' Iranian delegation in Doha for ceasefire-extension talks; 60-day MOU + Hormuz reopening framework holds. Baghaei: 'We have reached conclusions on a large portion of the issues, but no one can claim that the signing of an agreement is imminent.' IRAN INTERNET PARTIAL RESTORATION on Day 88 after 87 days — NetBlocks (per UPI): 'partial restoration to Internet connectivity in #Iran on day 88, after 2,093 hours of near-total isolation from international networks, the longest nationwide Internet shutdown in modern history'; 1st VP Aref: 'the first step toward free and regulated access to cyberspace has been taken'; decision taken May 25 at Supreme Council of Cyberspace. LEBANON: IDF airstrike on Mashghara village (Bekaa Valley) late May 25/overnight killed 11 (Lebanese MoH) / 12 (state NNA / AP, 12 bodies pulled from rubble) including a woman and two girls (Lebanese MoH via Antiwar.com). Al Jazeera correspondent Zeina Khodr: 'at least 10 attacks in the span of half an hour on an area with residential buildings.' Part of 76 IDF airstrikes on Lebanon May 25 (Antiwar.com). Netanyahu authorized intensified Hezbollah operations after Hezbollah drone killed IDF reservist Staff Sgt. Noam Hamburger; US Amb. Huckabee approved expansion but warned Israel 'not to bring down buildings in Beirut' (Channel 12). Lebanon/Israel direct military talks set for May 29 in Washington. Lebanese MoH X post May 26: 34 killed in past 24h — implied cumulative ~3,219 (FLAG: dashboard cumulative still 3,185 pending reconciliation). MARKETS: S&P 500 +0.61% to record 7,519.12 (45.65 pts); Nasdaq +1.19% to record 26,656.18; Dow -0.23% to 50,461.68 (-118.02 pts); Russell 2000 2,869.23; VIX 16.59. Rally led by Micron +19% — UBS hiked PT, market cap topped $1T for first time (+200% YTD, +800% past 12 months); semiconductor surge (AMD +6%, On Semi +9%, Western Digital +9%, SMH ETF 52-wk high +3%). Polymarket May 26: 91% probability S&P opens higher — resolved Yes. The Conference Board (May 26 release) Consumer Confidence 93.1 (-0.7 from upwardly revised 93.8; survey May 1–19); Chief Economist Dana M. Peterson: 'Consumer confidence edged downward in May as the inflationary impacts of the war in the Middle East intensified… References to prices and oil and gas increased in frequency for a second consecutive month, while mentions of war, geopolitics, and conflict remained elevated.' LNW CIO Ron Albahary (CNBC): investors 'pathologically optimistic.' OIL: Brent (ICE Jul'26) settle $99.58 (+3.58%, +$3.43) on strikes; WTI (NYMEX Jul'26) settle $93.89 (-2.81% vs Friday May 22 $96.60, no Monday settle due to Memorial Day); Brent-WTI spread widened to $5.69. AAA national gas $4.491 (-1.6¢ d/d), GasBuddy $4.45 (-6.6¢ w/w); diesel $5.571. Patrick De Haan: 'Average gasoline prices declined in 40 states over the last week as falling oil prices helped offset earlier price cycling… Much of the decline came after renewed optimism surrounding a potential U.S.-Iran agreement pushed oil prices lower.' HORMUZ: IRGC Navy claim (Mehr) 25 vessels coordinated May 26 (~25% of ~100/day Kpler baseline); US Navy reportedly resumed escorting tankers per Trading Economics. COST: stepped up to $200M/day midpoint reflecting overnight munitions consumption (CSIS Cancian model: $100M ceasefire floor → $500M active ceiling). Cumulative range: Pentagon $29B → Semler/SPRI $71.8B → Watson/Brown $40B in consumer fuel ALONE. Trump Cabinet meeting at Camp David scheduled Wednesday May 27 (WH official to CNBC).

Day 89 — TRUMP 'FINISH THE JOB' AT WHITE HOUSE CABINET MEETING; NEW US AIRSTRIKE ON A SOUTHERN-IRAN MILITARY SITE + MULTIPLE DRONE INTERCEPTS; IRAN FIRES BALLISTIC MISSILE AT KUWAIT (10:17 PM ET, INTERCEPTED) — CENTCOM: 'EGREGIOUS CEASEFIRE VIOLATION'; S&P 2ND STRAIGHT RECORD 7,520.36 (+0.02%), DOW RECORD 50,644.28; JULY WTI SETTLES $88.68 (-5.55%, 5-WEEK LOW) ON DEAL OPTIMISM, BRENT ~$93.91; LEBANON +~31 ON ONE OF THE HEAVIEST ISRAELI BOMBING DAYS IN WEEKS, ISRAEL ORDERS FORCED DISPLACEMENT OF ALL SOUTH LEBANON: Trump (Cabinet meeting): 'We're not satisfied with it, but we will be. Either that, or we'll have to just finish the job'; ruled out sanctions relief for HEU ('Not sanctions relief, no') and said he won't rush ('I don't care about the midterms'). US carried out a new airstrike on a southern-Iran military site threatening US forces and commercial Hormuz traffic + intercepted multiple Iranian drones (US official via ABC/CNN). At 10:17 p.m. ET Iran fired a ballistic missile at Kuwait, intercepted by Kuwaiti forces; CENTCOM: 'This egregious ceasefire violation… occurred hours after Iranian forces launched five one-way attack drones that posed a clear threat in and near the Strait of Hormuz.' IRGC claimed it struck a US air base in Kuwait. MARKETS: S&P 500 7,520.36 (+0.02%) record close; Dow 50,644.28 record; Nasdaq 26,674.73; July WTI settled $88.68 (-5.55%), Brent ~$93.91 — CNBC: oil 'betting on a swift end.' LEBANON: ~31 killed (Tyre, Saida, Nabatieh); IDF struck 150+ Hezbollah sites; forced-displacement order for ALL of south Lebanon; Netanyahu: forces advanced 'beyond the yellow line.' Lebanese cumulative 3,213 (MoH May 26) / 3,269 (CNN May 27). LMT $531.14. Iran MoH toll held at 3,468 (no new figure since May 20).

Day 90 — TENTATIVE 60-DAY US-IRAN MOU REACHED BY NEGOTIATORS (UNSIGNED; TRUMP APPROVAL PENDING; IRAN/TASNIM DENIES FINALIZATION); OVERNIGHT US STRIKE ON IRGC DRONE GROUND-CONTROL STATION AT BANDAR ABBAS + 4-5 DRONE SHOOTDOWNS NEAR HORMUZ; IRGC WARNING SHOTS AT 4 HORMUZ VESSELS; S&P 3RD STRAIGHT RECORD 7,563.63 (+0.58%); OIL REBOUNDS ~2.5% (BRENT ~$96.63, WTI >$91); AAA GAS $4.426; SHUWAYFAT STRIKE KILLS A WOMAN, HER BABY, AND A SYRIAN CHILD: Axios reported US and Iranian negotiators reached a tentative 60-day MOU — unrestricted Hormuz shipping (no tolls/harassment), Iran de-mines within 30 days, US blockade lifted proportionally, Iran pledges no nuclear weapon, US to discuss sanctions relief + frozen assets — but it needs Trump's approval and Iran had NOT confirmed; Tasnim denied finalization. VP Vance: 'making some progress' but 'not there yet.' Treasury Sec. Bessent declined to confirm details, threatened Oman with sanctions over Hormuz tolls. KINETIC: overnight US shot down 4-5 Iranian attack drones near Hormuz + struck an IRGC drone ground-control station at Bandar Abbas; IRGC Navy fired warning shots at 4 vessels attempting unauthorized transit. MARKETS: S&P 500 7,563.63 (+0.58%) record; Nasdaq 26,917.47 (+0.91%); Dow ~50,669; Brent rebounded ~2.48% toward ~$96.63, WTI back above $91 — still tracking a 2nd straight weekly decline; AAA gas eased to $4.426; LMT $537.21; UBS raised its Brent forecast to $105. LEBANON: Shuwayfat strike (south of Beirut) killed a woman, her baby daughter, and a Syrian child (+3), wounded 15; Sidon apartment-building strike; IDF claimed 135 Hezbollah targets in 24h. Israeli reservist Sgt. Rotem Yanai killed by a Hezbollah drone. COST: Pentagon official held ~$29B (Hurst); Bilmes ~$2B/day, ~$1T projected lifetime; AEI ~$260/household.

Day 91 — TENTATIVE 60-DAY CEASEFIRE EXTENSION REACHED; TRUMP IN SITUATION ROOM FOR 'FINAL DETERMINATION'; BLOCKADE TO BE LIFTED; OIL FALLS ~2%; DOW TOPS 51,000 FOR FIRST TIME. US-Iran negotiators agreed a tentative 60-day ceasefire extension (pending Trump sign-off); Iran says no deal yet and refuses nuclear talks. Trump in the White House Situation Room for a 'final determination'; posted demands (Iran never to have a nuclear weapon; Hormuz immediately open with no tolls; mines removed/detonated; enriched 'nuclear dust' destroyed with IAEA; 'no money will be exchanged, until further notice') and announced the US naval blockade 'will now be lifted' and stranded ships 'may start the process of heading home.' Iran foreign ministry: 'we are focused on ending the war, and there are no negotiations on the nuclear issue.' Speaker/negotiator Ghalibaf: 'we have no trust in guarantees or words — only actions are the measure.' MARKETS: S&P 500 7,580.08 (+0.22%) — 4th straight record + 9th straight weekly gain, longest since 2023; Dow ~51,037 (+0.73%) — first close above 51,000 ever; Nasdaq ~26,972 (+0.26%); Russell 2000 ~2,919 (-0.60%); VIX 15.41. OIL FELL ~2% at 5-6 week lows on deal news — Brent $91.82 (-0.95%), WTI ~$87.36 (-1.73%); Brent ended May -17%, worst month since 2020. AAA gas $4.391 — biggest one-day drop since Nov 22, 2008. Defense names (RTX/LMT/NOC) under pressure; ITA -12% since early March. CENTCOM blockade tally as of May 29: 115 commercial vessels redirected (vs 100 May 23), 4 disabled. COST: Pentagon official ~$29B (Brown Costs of War); ~$72B independent through ~60 days (Semler/SPRI); Bilmes ~$1T projected lifetime; +$40B+ extra fuel costs to U.S. consumers.
history.note: US-Iran negotiators agreed a tentative 60-day ceasefire extension (pending Trump sign-off); Iran says no deal yet and refuses nuclear talks. Dow tops 51,000 for first time.

history.headline: Day 92 (May 30, Saturday) — NO SIGNED MOU; TRUMP 'TOUGHENED' TERMS (NYT) / 'SEVERAL AMENDMENTS' (AXIOS); IRAN (BAGHAEI, GHALIBAF) SAYS NO AGREEMENT EXISTS; HEGSETH AT SHANGRI-LA DIALOGUE — TRUMP $1.5T DEFENSE PLAN, 3.5% GDP ALLIED ASK; OMAN MARITIME SECURITY CENTRE REPORTS SUSPECTED FLOATING MINE IN HORMUZ (NOT US-CONFIRMED); BLOOMBERG DISCLOSES MAY 27 KUWAIT FALLOUT: ~5 US WIA + 2 MQ-9 REAPERS HIT BY DEBRIS; +1 IDF KIA IN SOUTHERN LEBANON. MARKETS CLOSED weekend — Friday closes carry: S&P 7,580.06; Dow 51,032.46; Brent $92.05; WTI $87.36. AAA gas $4.35/gal (down 4¢ d/d; biggest one-day drop since Nov 2008 carries into weekend). DAILY BURN at ~$90M Cancian/CSIS floor on a weekend with no major kinetics. CENTCOM ceasefire-holding posture maintained; Caine: 'low-level kinetics… below the threshold of restarting major combat.' Iran's IRGC Mohsen Rezaei: Trump 'betraying diplomacy for the third time.' Lebanon ≥3,300 (LB MoPH per NPR May 30); UN peacekeepers: Israel 3,000+ strikes vs Hezbollah 187 'since last Sunday'; PM Salam (May 30) accused Israel of 'scorched-earth policy.'
history.note: No signed deal; Trump toughened terms; Hegseth at Shangri-La unveils Trump's $1.5T defense plan; suspected Hormuz mine reported by Oman; Bloomberg discloses ~5 US WIA + 2 MQ-9 hit in May 27 Kuwait strike.

history.headline: Day 93 (May 31, Sunday) — CEASEFIRE HOLDING (FRAGILE) — NO EXTENSION SIGNED. TRUMP TELLS FOX NEWS HE IS 'IN NO HURRY' AND THE ONLY GUARANTEE HE REQUIRES IS 'NO NUCLEAR WEAPONS'; IRAN REASSERTS HORMUZ CONTROL VIA KHATAM AL-ANBIYA ORDER (ALL VESSELS TO USE DESIGNATED ROUTES + OBTAIN IRGC NAVY AUTHORIZATION); IRGC CLAIMS DOWNING A US DRONE (UNVERIFIED); IRAN UNVEILS '27 RAJAB' NAVAL ATTACK CRAFT IN TEHRAN; US DISABLES GAMBIA-FLAGGED SHIP (BLOCKADE TALLY +1, NOW 5); IRAN STATE MEDIA $12BN FROZEN-ASSET CLAIM CALLED 'FABRICATION' BY WH; CONGRESS ADVANCES US-ISRAELI MILITARY INTEGRATION. LEBANON MoPH (May 31 bulletin): 3,412 killed / 10,269 wounded / 127 healthcare workers killed (+112 vs Day 92 ≥3,300). NO new US KIA — 13 cumulative (CENTCOM). MARKETS CLOSED weekend; Friday May 29 closes carry: S&P 7,580.06, Dow 51,032.46, Brent $92.05, WTI $87.36. AAA gas $4.35/gal (held). DAILY BURN ~$95M on Cancian/CSIS floor. Iran Ghalibaf (IRNA May 31): Tehran 'will not approve any agreement until we are sure that we have secured the rights of the Iranian people.' Watch Monday Jun 1 open for deal-collapse risk priced (energy higher / equities lower) or a Trump sign-off (the reverse).
history.note: Trump 'in no hurry' (Fox/Lara Trump); Iran reasserts Hormuz control via Khatam al-Anbiya order; IRGC claims downing US drone (UNVERIFIED); Iran unveils 27 Rajab naval craft; US disables Gambia-flagged ship; LB MoPH 3,412 killed.

history.headline: Day 94 (June 1, Monday) — CEASEFIRE STRAINED: IRAN SUSPENDS INDIRECT TALKS. IRGC-linked Tasnim says Tehran is 'opening other fronts' (citing Israeli actions in Lebanon + US ceasefire violations) and suspends document exchange; FM spokesman Baqaei: a Lebanon ceasefire is 'an essential condition for any deal.' Trump counters ('continuing, at a rapid pace') and tells CNBC's Eamon Javers 'I really don't care. I couldn't care less.' KUWAIT intercepts 'hostile' Iranian missile/drone fire (FM holds Iran 'fully responsible'); IRGC claims it struck 'the air base from which the attack originated' (UNVERIFIED). MARKETS: oil SURGES on conflict fears — Brent settles $94.98 (+4.24%), WTI $92.54 (+5.93%); S&P 500 RECORD 7,599.96 (+0.26%), Nasdaq 27,086.81 (+0.42%), Dow 51,078.88 (+0.09%) — all records on a tech rally (Nvidia +6%). AAA gas $4.322. ITEP: consumer fuel burden cumulative ~$46.5B / $347.72 per household (May 31). Two-carrier Arabian Sea posture (Bush + Lincoln) holds per USNI June 1.
history.note: Iran suspends indirect talks (Tasnim, 'opening other fronts'); Trump 'rapid pace'; Kuwait intercepts Iranian missile/drone fire, IRGC claims retaliatory strike (base UNVERIFIED); oil surges (Brent $94.98 +4.24%, WTI $92.54 +5.93%); S&P record 7,599.96; gas $4.322; ITEP $46.5B/$347.72 per household.

history.headline: Day 95 (June 2, Tuesday) — TALKS 'BACK ON TRACK': TRUMP TELLS ABC NEWS A DEAL TO REOPEN HORMUZ + EXTEND THE CEASEFIRE IS REACHABLE 'OVER THE NEXT WEEK'; a regional source tells CNN negotiations are 'back on track' — a partial walk-back of June 1's suspension. Ceasefire status: ACTIVE BUT TALKS SUSPENDED (limbo, not collapse). IRAN's internet partially restored after a ~3-month blackout; Pars Oil & Gas restored production at three offshore platforms. LEBANON MoPH (June 2 bulletin): 3,433 killed / 10,395 wounded (+21 vs May 31) after June 1 fighting (Beaufort Castle captured; Dahiyeh strikes; Israeli strike near a Tyre hospital — UN 'deeply alarmed'). MARKETS: oil holds near $95 Brent intraday; US equities near record highs. NO new US/Iranian fatalities; daily burn ~$95M. Next review trigger: Trump's stated 'next week' window (~June 9).
history.note: Talks 'back on track' (CNN regional source); Trump tells ABC a deal is reachable 'over the next week'; Iran's internet partially restored; Pars restores 3 offshore platforms; Lebanon 3,433/10,395 (June 2); oil near $95; equities near records.

history.headline: Day 96 (June 3, Wednesday) — KINETIC EXCHANGES INTENSIFY; HOUSE REBUKES TRUMP 215-208: an Iranian drone/missile strike on Kuwait International Airport killed one Indian national and wounded 63+ (a terminal was briefly closed); the US struck an Iranian oil tanker off Qeshm; Iran's missiles/drones at Kuwait and Bahrain were largely intercepted. The US House passed an Iran war-powers resolution 215-208 — the first successful such vote (four Republicans crossed; 60% public disapproval per PBS/NPR/Marist). MARKETS: oil climbed toward $100 (Brent ~$97.98, +2.1%) and the S&P 500 snapped a nine-day record-setting win streak (-0.74%; Dow -1.21%, Nasdaq -0.89%); defense (LMT +14.9% YTD) and oil majors outperformed. Ceasefire 'tested' but holding; the 60-day extension MoU remains unsigned. Daily burn ~$150M. US KIA 13. Lebanon ~3,473 killed (+5 incl. a child).
history.note: Kuwait airport drone/missile strike kills 1 (Indian national), 63+ wounded; US strikes an Iranian tanker off Qeshm; House passes war-powers resolution 215-208; oil nears $100; S&P snaps a nine-day win streak (-0.74%); Lebanon ~3,473 (+5).

targets_struck.label: Cumulative targets struck (US+IL on Iran/proxies)
targets_struck.note: Day 96: Bumped +3 to reflect the June 2-3 US self-defense strikes on an Iranian military ground-control station at Qeshm Island, the June 3 Hellfire strike on an Iranian oil tanker off Qeshm, and associated one-way attack-drone shootdowns. CENTCOM's narrower count of strikes inside Iran exceeds 13,000 over the six weeks of major combat; this counter tracks the broader combined US+Israeli total. The US ended its naval blockade of Iranian ports May 29; CENTCOM tankers-disabled cum = 5. Adm. Brad Cooper prior reference: 'nearly 2,000' command-and-control strikes.
targets_struck.tooltip: CENTCOM/IDF strikes since Feb 28. Includes 900+ first-12-hour Operation Epic Fury strikes (US+IL). Excludes Iranian retaliation. CENTCOM blockade tally on Day 93: 115 commercial vessels redirected (May 29 carry; ~100 May 23), 5 disabled (Gambia-flagged ship +1 on May 31), 26 humanitarian permitted through under the naval blockade. Trump's May 29 Situation Room announcement that the blockade 'will now be lifted' has NOT been operationalized — over the weekend Trump 'toughened the terms' (NYT) and asked for 'several amendments' (Axios). Atlantic Council (May 15): US has expended >1,000 JASSMs, >1,000 Tomahawks, ~1,000 Patriot interceptors, ~45% of Precision Strike Missile stockpile and ~50% of THAAD interceptor stockpile. Cumulative US aircraft losses/damage: 42 (CRS via Stars and Stripes May 20) — would become 43-44 if the May 27 Bloomberg report of 2 MQ-9 Reapers hit at Ali Al Salem is confirmed. Tomahawk usage updates: WaPo reported >850 TLAMs in the first month, WSJ later updated to >1,000; Stars and Stripes: 'has fired more Tomahawk missiles during Operation Epic Fury than in any other military campaign in history,' ahead of Operation Iraqi Freedom (802) and Desert Storm (288) (CSIS, Cancian & Park).

us_kia.label: US service-member KIA
us_kia.note: Day 96: Unchanged at 13. No US KIA in the June 2-3 exchanges — the Qeshm strikes drew no US losses, and the Iranian missile/drone attacks on Kuwait and Bahrain were intercepted; the June 3 Kuwait airport strike killed an Indian national, not a US service member. 57-day streak of zero-combat-KIA days since the 4/7 ceasefire. CENTCOM/DCAS one-page also shows 14 (including 1 non-combat death).
us_kia.tooltip: Includes 7 servicemembers killed in opening Iranian retaliation wave + 6 USAF airmen in KC-135 crash in western Iraq. Composition: 6 USAF crew (March 13 KC-135 crash western Iraq, CENTCOM ruled non-hostile mid-air collision); 6 Kuwait Camp Arifjan drone attack March 1; 1 Saudi Arabia. US MIA 0. CENTCOM 13 KIA + 1 non-combat death; DCAS one-page shows 14. 10 civilian sailors of various nationalities killed in Hormuz-related incidents. Explicit EXECUTIVE CONFIRMATION by President Trump at Arlington National Cemetery May 25: 'In Operation Epic Fury, we lost 13 wonderful souls.' No US KIA in the May 30–31 weekend; the May 27 Iranian ballistic missile at Ali Al Salem (Kuwait) caused ~5 minor injuries per Bloomberg disclosure May 30 but no KIA.

us_wia.label: US WIA (independent est.)
us_wia.note: Day 96: Held at 527 (independent estimate). No new US wounded in the June 2-3 exchanges — the Kuwait and Bahrain missile/drone attacks were intercepted with no reported US casualties. Pentagon/DCAS official cumulative as of May 26: 409 WIA (~90% returned to duty); manifest §1a cites the CENTCOM-confirmed figure as ~365 (303 as of March 28), a narrower official basis than this independent 520-538 range. The Intercept alleges the official count undercounts by ~200+ non-hostile injuries.
us_wia.tooltip: Pentagon/DCAS official: 409 WIA as of May 26 (~90% returned to duty); 15 wounded were removed from the count on April 21 without explanation. Independent estimates (The Intercept / Wikipedia 2026 Iran war) range 520–538. The Intercept alleges the Pentagon figure undercounts by ~200+ non-hostile injuries. Manifest §1a range: ~140 (Pentagon, March 13) vs ~365 (CENTCOM, later trackers); last public CENTCOM figure 303 as of March 28. May 27 Ali Al Salem (Kuwait): a US official told CBS that 4 US service members + 3 contractors (7 total) suffered minor injuries from debris when Iran's Fateh-110 was intercepted by Kuwaiti air defenses; all returned to duty within 24 hours. Bloomberg (May 30) earlier cited ~5 wounded plus one MQ-9 Reaper destroyed and another seriously damaged (~$30M each). DISCREPANCY: GlobalSecurity.org Day-91 said 'no…US military casualties or asset damage' for the same intercept — treat as UNRESOLVED.

iranian_killed.label: Iranian dead (Iran MoH / Foundation of Martyrs, Apr 19)
iranian_killed.note: Day 96: No official Iran MoH update — figure held at 3,468 (Apr 19 Foundation of Martyrs count, now ~45 days old / effectively FROZEN). No verified new Iranian deaths in the June 2-3 exchanges, and none published for the June 2-3 Qeshm strikes (Iran issued no casualty tabulation). HRANA (US-based) documents 3,636+ (1,221 military, 1,701 civilian, 714 unclassified). Hengaw: 6,620 military killed (April 8 estimate; highest independent count). The gap between Iran MoH 3,468 and the independent counts remains politically consequential — the government continues to gate casualty data.
iranian_killed.tooltip: Iran's Foundation of Martyrs cumulative total = 3,468 as of Apr 19 (7 infants, 376 children, 496 women; 26,500+ injured). CONFLICTING RANGE (per manifest §9, do not synthesize): 3,468 (Iran MoH / Foundation of Martyrs — FROZEN since April 19 due to documented Iranian government information suppression) / 3,636+ (HRANA: 1,701 civ / 1,221 mil / 714 unclassified) / ~6,620 military KIA in Kurdish provinces by April 8 (Hengaw) / 7,650 cumulative (Hengaw 40-day report incl. 1,030 civilians) / 4,700+ security forces (Iran International) / 6,000+ IRGC (IDF claim). Iranian Red Crescent (May 22): aid workers rescued more than 7,200 people from rubble across US/Israeli attacks since the war began. The true toll is higher (per Hengaw, HRANA) given documented Iranian government concealment.

lebanese_killed.label: Lebanese dead (Lebanese MoPH, June 3; +5 incl. a child)
lebanese_killed.note: Day 96: Lebanese Ministry of Public Health cumulative reported at 3,468 killed / 10,577 wounded for March 2-June 2 (an upward revision from the 3,433 first logged June 2); +5 killed June 3, including a child, in Burj Shemali, Ebba, and Tibnin → ~3,473 cumulative. Jabal Amel Hospital in Tyre was damaged by an Israeli strike (June 2); MSF flagged a strike near Hiram Hospital the prior day. 127+ healthcare workers killed war-to-date.
lebanese_killed.tooltip: Lebanon war cumulative since March 2: ~3,473 killed / 10,577 wounded / 127+ healthcare workers killed (Lebanese Ministry of Public Health; the June-2 cumulative was revised up to 3,468, then +5 June 3). MoPH breakdown war-to-date: ≥211 children, nearly 300 women among the dead. Internal Hezbollah sources say 1,000+ fighters killed; IDF claims 1,700 killed. Israel (since March 2): 57 citizens/residents killed (28 soldiers incl. one off-duty and one friendly-fire, 28 civilians, 1 MoD contractor); 8,970+ injured incl. 1,191 military (Wikipedia casualties, June 3). Iraq: at least 118 killed; Iraqi Kurdistan hit by 196+ drone/missile attacks.

displaced.label: Displaced (Lebanon, UNHCR-based)
displaced.note: Day 96: Held at >1.2 million displaced in Lebanon (IOM/UN >1M; CSMonitor ~1.2M); UNHCR ~3.2M inside Iran (~1M households); WFP ~1.24M food-insecure. Continued Israeli strikes around Tyre (Burj Shemali, Ebba, Tibnin) and southern Lebanon sustain displacement pressure. Lebanon: 140,000+ in collective shelters; 147,823 crossed to Syria since March 1; ~68,000 Iranians fled to Türkiye, ~30,000 to Afghanistan.
displaced.tooltip: UNHCR / Lebanese government figures. IOM 1M+ displaced in Lebanon; 140,000+ in collective shelters; 147,823 crossed to Syria since March 1; CSMonitor ~1.2M as of May 7. UNHCR ~3.2M inside Iran (~1M households). ~68,000 Iranians fled to Türkiye, ~30,000 to Afghanistan. Cross-border into Syria: 306,888 Syrians + 64,865 Lebanese (May 2 baseline, carry-forward). 40,000+ homes destroyed in southern Lebanon; cumulative evacuation orders cover ~1,470 km² (~14% of national territory).

flights_cancelled.label: Cumulative flights cancelled (Gulf hubs, est.)
flights_cancelled.note: Day 96: Kuwait International Airport was struck June 3 — a terminal was severely damaged and the airport briefly closed before Kuwait Airways and Jazeera Airways resumed operations from a different terminal the same day. Aggregate held at ~8,000+. KLM Riyadh/Dammam/Dubai suspensions extended to June 28; Lufthansa Group Tel Aviv to June 30, Dubai to July 11 (The National, May 12).
flights_cancelled.tooltip: FlightAware running figures from war's first weeks: DXB ~4,000 / DOH 2,000+ / AUH 1,000+. Aggregate ~8,000+ remains conservative. AAA holiday-travel survey: 3.66M Americans projected to fly for Memorial Day weekend — a record despite ongoing disruption. Methodological note: 'flights affected' captures cancellations + diversions + multi-hour holds + reroutes + overflight disruptions across all regional FIRs. Gulf carriers continue suspended/rerouted ops; Dubai International at limited capacity.

children_killed.label: Children killed in Iran (UNICEF Mar 12 baseline + updates)
children_killed.note: Day 96: +1 child killed in Lebanon June 3 (Burj Shemali / Ebba / Tibnin). This counter tracks Iran (UNICEF Mar 12 baseline 200, unchanged June 3). Combined regional child toll is 413+ per Time (April): 248 Iran + 165 Lebanon. Iran MoH 376 children dead (Apr 19 cumulative; STALE ~45 days); Lebanese MoPH ≥211 children war-to-date.
children_killed.tooltip: Multiple methodologies; UNICEF figure is the most-cited international baseline. Iran MoH (via Al Jazeera tracker; STALE since Apr 19): 376 children killed (incl. 7 infants), 496 women. HRANA: ≥254 children among Iranian civilian dead (Apr 7). Lebanese MoPH: ≥210-211 children among the dead (war-to-date breakdown May 19); 98+ children killed in Lebanon per manifest. UNICEF (Mar 12): >1,100 children killed/injured regionally (200 Iran + 91 Lebanon + 4 Israel + 1 Kuwait subset) — STALE. Israeli child casualties tracked separately.
